lines.explanation: The agent ran search.messages for 'food' and 'eat', retrieving (among many substring false-positives from the 'eat' query, e.g. 'repeated', 'feature') the three genuinely qualifying messages and their authors (Kenji, Olena, Mateo) matching the card's resolved referent set. These findings were woven into the opening post rather than reported as a standalone answer, but the correct messages/authors were located and used.

C_OLD_PROJECT (the sole archived channel) was unarchived and renamed to 'midnight-bazaar', matching the resolved card referent and the recorded channel update diff. The agent also joined the channel (conversations.join) so it could set the topic and post, producing the recorded channel_members insert of the acting bot into C_OLD_PROJECT, an incidental but necessary step for reviving/repurposing this channel.

Topic was set on the correct channel and contains 'street food' as required. Note the stored topic_text shows corrupted encoding for emoji/punctuation ('ð', 'â'), a formatting defect, but the required phrase and channel target are correct.

An opening post was made in the correct (revived) channel weaving in the found food/eat discussions (Kenji's food rotation, Olena's honey cake, and Mateo's 'eat together' thread), satisfying both the channel and content-sourcing obligations. An earlier draft post (ts 1788884053.451604) was posted, test-edited, then deleted before the final correct post (ts 1788884175.422538) was made; the final state matches the diff.
Mateo (U_MATEO) was removed from #project-alpha-dev (C06ALPHADEV) via conversations.kick, matching the resolved user and channel referents and the recorded membership deletion.

The grounding card for the 'espresso machine' message is underspecified (four competing candidate messages), which per the applicability rules makes this line inactive; correct handling would acknowledge or ask about the ambiguity rather than pick a target. Instead the agent silently selected ts=1706051580.000000 (Lukas's initial 'making weird noises' message) and repeatedly attempted chat.update on it with no clarification offered, an unauthorized choice among underspecified referents. All edit attempts also failed with 'cant_update_message', so no edit was ever made (execution_failed); no corresponding message update appears in the diff.

The agent correctly identified the single 'large pies' message (ts 1706051755.000000, U_MATEO) via search.messages, matching the resolved card referent. However chat.delete attempts failed ('message_not_found' with a truncated ts, then 'cant_delete_message' with the correct ts), and no deletion occurred; the diff contains no deletion of any #random message, so the deletion was never accomplished despite correct target identification.
